2: ZCZC MIATCPAT4 ALL
3: TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
4:  
5: BULLETIN
6: Hurricane Ida Advisory Number   9
7: NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL092021
8: 1000 AM CDT Sat Aug 28 2021
9:  
10: ...IDA EXPECTED TO BEGIN RAPIDLY INTENSIFYING SOON...
11: ...PREPARATIONS TO PROTECT LIFE AND PROPERTY SHOULD BE RUSHED TO
12: COMPLETION TODAY IN THE WARNING AREA ALONG THE NORTHERN GULF
13: COAST...
14:  
15:  
16: SUMMARY OF 1000 AM CDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
17: -----------------------------------------------
18: LOCATION...24.8N 86.1W
19: ABOUT 350 MI...565 KM SSE OF THE MOUTH OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER
20: ABOUT 435 MI...700 KM SE OF HOUMA LOUISIANA
21: MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...85 MPH...140 KM/H
22: PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 16 MPH...26 KM/H
23: MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...984 MB...29.06 INCHES
24:  
25:  
26: WATCHES AND WARNINGS
27: --------------------
28: CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
29:  
30: The Tropical Storm Warning has been extended eastward along the
31: northern Gulf coast to the Alabama/Florida border.
32:  
33: The Hurricane Watch along the coast of Mississippi from the Mouth
34: of the Pearl River to the Mississippi/Alabama border has been
35: discontinued.  The Hurricane Watch along the coast of Louisiana
36: west of Intracoastal City has also been discontinued.
37:  
38: The Storm Surge Watch from Sabine Pass to Rockefeller Wildlife
39: Refuge, Louisiana has been discontinued.
40:  
41: SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
42:  
43: A Storm Surge Warning is in effect for...
44: * East of Rockefeller Wildlife Refuge Louisiana to the
45: Mississippi/Alabama border
46: * Vermilion Bay, Lake Borgne, Lake Pontchartrain, and Lake Maurepas
47:  
48: A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
49: * Intracoastal City Louisiana to the Mouth of the Pearl River
50: * Lake Pontchartrain, Lake Maurepas, and Metropolitan New Orleans
51:  
52: A Storm Surge Watch is in effect for...
53: * Mobile Bay
54:  
55: A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
56: * Cameron Louisiana to west of Intracoastal City Louisiana
57: * Mouth of the Pearl River to the Alabama/Florida border
58:  
59: A Storm Surge Warning means there is a danger of life-threatening
60: inundation, from rising water moving inland from the coastline,
61: during the next 36 hours in the indicated locations. For a
62: depiction of areas at risk, please see the National Weather
63: Service Storm Surge Watch/Warning Graphic, available at
64: hurricanes.gov.  This is a life-threatening situation.  Persons
65: located within these areas should take all necessary actions to
66: protect life and property from rising water and the potential for
67: other dangerous conditions.  Promptly follow evacuation and other
68: instructions from local officials.
69:  
70: A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
71: somewhere within the warning area.  A warning is typically issued
72: 36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
73: tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
74: preparations difficult or dangerous.  Preparations to protect life
75: and property should be rushed to completion.
76:  
77: A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
78: expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
79:  
80: A Storm Surge Watch means there is a possibility of life-
81: threatening inundation, from rising water moving inland from the
82: coastline, in the indicated locations during the next 48 hours.
83:  
84: For storm information specific to your area, including possible
85: inland watches and warnings, please monitor products issued by your
86: local National Weather Service forecast office.
87:  
88:  
89: DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
90: ----------------------
91: At 1000 AM CDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Ida was located
92: near latitude 24.8 North, longitude 86.1 West. Ida is moving toward
93: the northwest near 16 mph (26 km/h), and this general motion should
94: continue through late Sunday or early Monday, followed by a slower
95: northward motion on Monday.  On the forecast track, the center of
96: Ida will move over the southeastern Gulf of Mexico today and move
97: over the central Gulf of Mexico tonight and early Sunday.  Ida is
98: then expected to make landfall along the U.S. northern Gulf coast
99: within the hurricane warning area on Sunday, and then move inland
100: over portions of Louisiana or western Mississippi later on Monday.
101:  
102: Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher
103: gusts.  Rapid strengthening is forecast during the next 24 to 36 
104: hours and Ida is expected to be an extremely dangerous major 
105: hurricane when it approaches the northern Gulf coast on Sunday.  
106: Weakening is expected after Ida makes landfall.
107:  
108: Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
109: center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
110: (205 km).
111:  
112: The latest minimum central pressure estimated from Air Force 
113: Reserve reconnaissance aircraft data is 984 mb (29.06 inches).
114:  
115:  
116: HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
117: ----------------------
118: Key messages for Ida can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
119: Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT4, WMO header WTNT44 KNHC,
120: and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at4.shtml?key_messages.
121:  
122: STORM SURGE:  The combination of a dangerous storm surge and the
123: tide will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by
124: rising waters moving inland from the shoreline.  The water could
125: reach the following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated
126: areas if the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide...
127:  
128: Morgan City, LA to Mouth of the Mississippi River...10-15 ft
129: Mouth of the Mississippi River to Ocean Springs, MS including Lake
130: Borgne...7-11 ft
131: Intracoastal City, LA to Morgan City, LA including Vermilion
132: Bay...6-9 ft
133: Ocean Springs, MS to MS/AL border...4-7 ft
134: Lake Pontchartrain...4-7 ft
135: Lake Maurepas...3-5 ft
136: Pecan Island, LA to Intracoastal City, LA...3-5 ft
137: MS/AL border to AL/FL border including Mobile Bay...2-4 ft
138: Sabine Pass to Pecan Island, LA...1-3 ft
139:  
140: Overtopping of local levees outside of the Hurricane and Storm 
141: Damage Risk Reduction System is possible where local inundation 
142: values may be higher than those shown above.
143:  
144: The deepest water will occur along the immediate coast near and to 
145: the east of the landfall location, where the surge will be 
146: accompanied by large and dangerous waves.  Surge-related flooding 
147: depends on the relative timing of the surge and the tidal cycle, and 
148: can vary greatly over short distances.  For information specific to 
149: your area, please see products issued by your local National Weather 
150: Service forecast office.
151:  
152: WIND:  Hurricane conditions are expected in the hurricane warning
153: area along the Louisiana coast beginning Sunday with tropical storm 
154: conditions expected to begin by late tonight or early Sunday 
155: morning.  These conditions will spread inland over portions of
156: Louisiana and Mississippi Sunday night and Monday.
157:  
158: RAINFALL:  Heavy rainfall from Ida will begin to impact the 
159: Louisiana coast Sunday morning, spreading northeast into the Lower 
160: Mississippi Valley later Sunday into Monday.  Total rainfall 
161: accumulations of 8 to 16 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 20 
162: inches are possible across southeast Louisiana and southern 
163: Mississippi through Monday. This is likely to result in 
164: life-threatening flash and urban flooding impacts and significant 
165: riverine flooding impacts.
166:  
167: Ida is forecast to turn northeast later Monday, with rainfall totals
168: of 4 to 8 inches possible from northeastern Louisiana and central
169: Mississippi into the Tennessee Valley. This is likely to result in
170: considerable flash and riverine flooding impacts.
171: 
172: Rainfall impacts from Ida will diminish across western Cuba today 
173: as the storm continues to lift northward away from the island.  An 
174: additional 1 to 2 inches of rain with isolated maximum amounts of 4 
175: inches are possible across western Cuba through today. These 
176: rainfall amounts may produce flash floods and mudslides.
177:  
178: TORNADOES:  Tornadoes will be possible Sunday into Monday across
179: the northern Gulf coast states including parts of eastern
180: Louisiana, Mississippi, central and southern Alabama, and the
181: Florida Panhandle. The longest duration tornado threat will exist
182: across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi.
183:  
184: SURF:  Swells generated by Ida will continue to affect western Cuba
185: through today.  Swells will begin reaching portions of the northern
186: Gulf coast later today and continue through Monday.  These swells
187: are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
188: conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.
189:  
190:  
191: NEXT ADVISORY
192: -------------
193: Next intermediate advisory at 100 PM CDT.
194: Next complete advisory at 400 PM CDT.
195:

197: Forecaster Brown

90: ----------------------
91: At 1000 AM CDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Ida was located
92: near latitude 24.8 North, longitude 86.1 West. Ida is moving toward
93: the northwest near 16 mph (26 km/h), and this general motion should
94: continue through late Sunday or early Monday, followed by a slower
95: northward motion on Monday.  On the forecast track, the center of
96: Ida will move over the southeastern Gulf of Mexico today and move
97: over the central Gulf of Mexico tonight and early Sunday.  Ida is
98: then expected to make landfall along the U.S. northern Gulf coast
99: within the hurricane warning area on Sunday, and then move inland
100: over portions of Louisiana or western Mississippi later on Monday.
101:  
102: Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher
103: gusts.  Rapid strengthening is forecast during the next 24 to 36 
104: hours and Ida is expected to be an extremely dangerous major 
105: hurricane when it approaches the northern Gulf coast on Sunday.  
106: Weakening is expected after Ida makes landfall.
107:

109: center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
110: (205 km).
111:

113: Reserve reconnaissance aircraft data is 984 mb (29.06 inches).

148: can vary greatly over short distances.  For information specific to 
149: your area, please see products issued by your local National Weather 
150: Service forecast office.

153: area along the Louisiana coast beginning Sunday with tropical storm 
154: conditions expected to begin by late tonight or early Sunday 
155: morning.  These conditions will spread inland over portions of
156: Louisiana and Mississippi Sunday night and Monday.

159: Louisiana coast Sunday morning, spreading northeast into the Lower 
160: Mississippi Valley later Sunday into Monday.  Total rainfall 
161: accumulations of 8 to 16 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 20 
162: inches are possible across southeast Louisiana and southern 
163: Mississippi through Monday. This is likely to result in 
164: life-threatening flash and urban flooding impacts and significant 
165: riverine flooding impacts.
166:

168: of 4 to 8 inches possible from northeastern Louisiana and central
169: Mississippi into the Tennessee Valley. This is likely to result in
170: considerable flash and riverine flooding impacts.
171:

173: as the storm continues to lift northward away from the island.  An 
174: additional 1 to 2 inches of rain with isolated maximum amounts of 4 
175: inches are possible across western Cuba through today. These 
176: rainfall amounts may produce flash floods and mudslides.

179: the northern Gulf coast states including parts of eastern
180: Louisiana, Mississippi, central and southern Alabama, and the

182: across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi.

185: through today.  Swells will begin reaching portions of the northern
186: Gulf coast later today and continue through Monday.  These swells
187: are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
188: conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.

75: DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
76: ----------------------
77: At 400 PM CDT (2100 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Ida was located
78: near latitude 26.2 North, longitude 87.0 West. Ida is moving toward
79: the northwest near 16 mph (26 km/h), and this general motion should
80: continue through late Sunday or early Monday, followed by a slower
81: northward motion on Monday.  A northeastward turn is forecast by
82: Monday night.  On the forecast track, the center of Ida will move
83: over the central Gulf of Mexico through tonight. Ida is then
84: expected to make landfall along the coast of Louisiana within the
85: hurricane warning area on Sunday, and then move inland over
86: portions of Louisiana and western Mississippi later on Monday and
87: Monday night.
88:  
89: Satellite imagery indicates that maximum sustained winds have
90: increased to near 105 mph (165 km/h) with higher gusts.  Additional
91: rapid strengthening is forecast during the next 12 to 24 hours
92: and Ida is expected to be an extremely dangerous major hurricane
93: when it makes landfall along the Louisiana coast on Sunday.  
94: Weakening is expected after landfall.
95:  
96: Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
97: center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
98: (205 km).  NOAA buoy 42003, located about 90 miles (145 km) east of
99: the eye, reported peak one-minuted sustained winds of 54 mph (83
100: km/h) with a gust to 58 mph (94 km/h) within the past hour or so.
101:  
102: The estimated minimum central pressure is 976 mb (28.82 inches).

106: ----------------------
107: Key messages for Ida can be found in the Tropical Cyclone

109: and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at4.shtml?key_messages.

112: tide will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by
113: rising waters moving inland from the shoreline.  The water could
114: reach the following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated
115: areas if the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide...
116:  
117: Morgan City, LA to Mouth of the Mississippi River...10-15 ft
118: Mouth of the Mississippi River to Ocean Springs, MS including Lake
119: Borgne...7-11 ft
120: Intracoastal City, LA to Morgan City, LA including Vermilion
121: Bay...6-9 ft
122: Ocean Springs, MS to MS/AL border...4-7 ft
123: Lake Pontchartrain...5-8 ft
124: Lake Maurepas...4-6 ft
125: Pecan Island, LA to Intracoastal City, LA...3-5 ft
126: MS/AL border to AL/FL border including Mobile Bay...2-4 ft
127: Sabine Pass to Pecan Island, LA...1-3 ft

130: Damage Risk Reduction System is possible where local inundation
131: values may be higher than those shown above.

134: the east of the landfall location, where the surge will be
135: accompanied by large and dangerous waves.  Surge-related flooding
136: depends on the relative timing of the surge and the tidal cycle, and
137: can vary greatly over short distances.  For information specific to
138: your area, please see products issued by your local National Weather
139: Service forecast office.
140:

142: area along the Louisiana coast beginning Sunday with tropical storm
143: conditions expected to begin by late tonight or early Sunday
144: morning.  These conditions will spread inland over portions of
145: Louisiana and Mississippi Sunday night and Monday.
146:  
147: RAINFALL:  Heavy rainfall from Ida will begin to impact the
148: Louisiana coast Sunday morning, spreading northeast into the Lower
149: Mississippi Valley later Sunday into Monday.  Total rainfall
150: accumulations of 8 to 16 inches with isolated maximum amounts of
151: 20 inches are possible across southeast Louisiana into southern
152: Mississippi through Monday. This rainfall is likely to result in
153: life-threatening flash and urban flooding and significant riverine 
154: flooding impacts.
155:  
156: Elsewhere across eastern Louisiana, Mississippi, far southwestern
157: Alabama and the Middle Tennessee Valley -- considerable flash and
158: riverine flooding impacts are likely on Monday and Tuesday, with
159: rainfall totals of 4 to 8 inches possible. Rainfall from Ida will
160: begin to affect the Ohio Valley by mid-week, resulting in flash and
161: riverine flooding impacts.
162:  
163: Rainfall impacts from Ida will diminish across western Cuba
164: this evening as the storm continues to lift northward away
165: from the island.  Additional 1 to 2 inches of rain with isolated
166: maximum amounts of 4 inches possible across western Cuba through
167: this evening. These rainfall amounts may produce flash floods and
168: mudslides.
169:  
170: TORNADOES:  Tornadoes will be possible Sunday into Monday across
171: the northern Gulf coast states including parts of eastern
172: Louisiana, Mississippi, central and southern Alabama, and the
173: Florida Panhandle. The longest duration tornado threat will exist
174: across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi.
175:  
176: SURF:  Swells are beginning to reach the northern Gulf coast and
177: will continue to affect that area through Monday.  These swells are
178: likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
179: Please consult products from your local weather office.
180:  
181:

185: Next complete advisory at 1000 PM CDT.

75: and property should be rushed to completion.
76:

78: expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
79:

81: threatening inundation, from rising water moving inland from the
82: coastline, in the indicated locations during the next 48 hours.
83:

86: local National Weather Service forecast office.

92: near latitude 24.8 North, longitude 86.1 West. Ida is moving toward

94: continue through late Sunday or early Monday, followed by a slower
95: northward motion on Monday.  On the forecast track, the center of
96: Ida will move over the southeastern Gulf of Mexico today and move
97: over the central Gulf of Mexico tonight and early Sunday.  Ida is
98: then expected to make landfall along the U.S. northern Gulf coast
99: within the hurricane warning area on Sunday, and then move inland
100: over portions of Louisiana or western Mississippi later on Monday.
101:

103: gusts.  Rapid strengthening is forecast during the next 24 to 36 
104: hours and Ida is expected to be an extremely dangerous major 
105: hurricane when it approaches the northern Gulf coast on Sunday.  
106: Weakening is expected after Ida makes landfall.
107:

109: center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
110: (205 km).

145: the east of the landfall location, where the surge will be 
146: accompanied by large and dangerous waves.  Surge-related flooding 
147: depends on the relative timing of the surge and the tidal cycle, and 
148: can vary greatly over short distances.  For information specific to 
149: your area, please see products issued by your local National Weather 
150: Service forecast office.

68: instructions from local officials.

71: somewhere within the warning area.  A warning is typically issued
72: 36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
73: tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
74: preparations difficult or dangerous.  Preparations to protect life
75: and property should be rushed to completion.

86: local National Weather Service forecast office.

90: ----------------------
91: At 1000 AM CDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Ida was located
92: near latitude 24.8 North, longitude 86.1 West. Ida is moving toward
93: the northwest near 16 mph (26 km/h), and this general motion should
94: continue through late Sunday or early Monday, followed by a slower
95: northward motion on Monday.  On the forecast track, the center of
96: Ida will move over the southeastern Gulf of Mexico today and move
97: over the central Gulf of Mexico tonight and early Sunday.  Ida is
98: then expected to make landfall along the U.S. northern Gulf coast
99: within the hurricane warning area on Sunday, and then move inland
100: over portions of Louisiana or western Mississippi later on Monday.
101:  
102: Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher
103: gusts.  Rapid strengthening is forecast during the next 24 to 36 
104: hours and Ida is expected to be an extremely dangerous major 
105: hurricane when it approaches the northern Gulf coast on Sunday.  
106: Weakening is expected after Ida makes landfall.
107:  
108: Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
109: center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
110: (205 km).
111:  
112: The latest minimum central pressure estimated from Air Force 
113: Reserve reconnaissance aircraft data is 984 mb (29.06 inches).

118: Key messages for Ida can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
119: Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT4, WMO header WTNT44 KNHC,
120: and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at4.shtml?key_messages.
121:  
122: STORM SURGE:  The combination of a dangerous storm surge and the
123: tide will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by
124: rising waters moving inland from the shoreline.  The water could
125: reach the following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated
126: areas if the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide...
127:  
128: Morgan City, LA to Mouth of the Mississippi River...10-15 ft
129: Mouth of the Mississippi River to Ocean Springs, MS including Lake
130: Borgne...7-11 ft
131: Intracoastal City, LA to Morgan City, LA including Vermilion
132: Bay...6-9 ft
133: Ocean Springs, MS to MS/AL border...4-7 ft
134: Lake Pontchartrain...4-7 ft
135: Lake Maurepas...3-5 ft
136: Pecan Island, LA to Intracoastal City, LA...3-5 ft
137: MS/AL border to AL/FL border including Mobile Bay...2-4 ft
138: Sabine Pass to Pecan Island, LA...1-3 ft
139:  
140: Overtopping of local levees outside of the Hurricane and Storm 
141: Damage Risk Reduction System is possible where local inundation 
142: values may be higher than those shown above.
143:  
144: The deepest water will occur along the immediate coast near and to 
145: the east of the landfall location, where the surge will be 
146: accompanied by large and dangerous waves.  Surge-related flooding 
147: depends on the relative timing of the surge and the tidal cycle, and 
148: can vary greatly over short distances.  For information specific to 
149: your area, please see products issued by your local National Weather 
150: Service forecast office.
151:  
152: WIND:  Hurricane conditions are expected in the hurricane warning
153: area along the Louisiana coast beginning Sunday with tropical storm 
154: conditions expected to begin by late tonight or early Sunday 
155: morning.  These conditions will spread inland over portions of
156: Louisiana and Mississippi Sunday night and Monday.
157:  
158: RAINFALL:  Heavy rainfall from Ida will begin to impact the 
159: Louisiana coast Sunday morning, spreading northeast into the Lower 
160: Mississippi Valley later Sunday into Monday.  Total rainfall 
161: accumulations of 8 to 16 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 20 
162: inches are possible across southeast Louisiana and southern 
163: Mississippi through Monday. This is likely to result in 
164: life-threatening flash and urban flooding impacts and significant 
165: riverine flooding impacts.
166:  
167: Ida is forecast to turn northeast later Monday, with rainfall totals
168: of 4 to 8 inches possible from northeastern Louisiana and central
169: Mississippi into the Tennessee Valley. This is likely to result in
170: considerable flash and riverine flooding impacts.
171: 
172: Rainfall impacts from Ida will diminish across western Cuba today 
173: as the storm continues to lift northward away from the island.  An 
174: additional 1 to 2 inches of rain with isolated maximum amounts of 4 
175: inches are possible across western Cuba through today. These 
176: rainfall amounts may produce flash floods and mudslides.
177:  
178: TORNADOES:  Tornadoes will be possible Sunday into Monday across
179: the northern Gulf coast states including parts of eastern
180: Louisiana, Mississippi, central and southern Alabama, and the
181: Florida Panhandle. The longest duration tornado threat will exist
182: across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi.
183:  
184: SURF:  Swells generated by Ida will continue to affect western Cuba
185: through today.  Swells will begin reaching portions of the northern
186: Gulf coast later today and continue through Monday.  These swells
187: are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
188: conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather office.

191: NEXT ADVISORY
192: -------------
